plan: This is a second-price auction (Vickrey auction) where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy. Since I pay the second-highest bid if I win (not my own bid), there's no incentive to shade my bid below my value - doing so only risks losing auctions I could have profitably won, without reducing what I'd pay. Bidding above value risks negative profit. Therefore, bidding exactly my value of $21 maximizes my expected profit.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors or their strategies. This is because your payment depends only on the second-highest bid, not your own bid, so there's no incentive to shade your bid. Bidding truthfully maximizes expected profit: if I win, I pay the second-highest bid (which is what I'd pay regardless of my exact bid above that), and bidding my true value ensures I only win when my value exceeds the price, guaranteeing non-negative profit whenever I win.

This is a second-price auction, where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy. Since I pay only the second-highest bid if I win, bidding my actual value of $13 ensures I never overpay and maximizes expected profit regardless of what others bid. Bidding lower risks losing profitable auctions, and bidding higher risks winning at a loss. I'll bid exactly $13.
